title: Capacity priming retrospective - Midwest edge (2027-03-09)
content:
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marta, Samir, Jamal, + on-call (Olivia)

Purpose: short retrospective on the Midwest edge capacity priming pilot (2-week window) and standup notes for next-phase actions. Capture signals, anomalies, and cross-team handoffs.

Quick summary:
- Pilot goal: reduce p95 cold-start token latency for p99 workloads in midwest region by pre-warming a small fraction of the fleet and measuring cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Window: 2027-02-22 -> 2027-03-08 (14 days).
- Key result: p95 token latency for heavy chat routes dropped 18% in the 03:00-09:00 local window when priming was active. 7% increase in baseline hourly GPU-hours due to steady-state idle warming.
- Incidents: 1 transient quota oversubscription event (2027-03-03 04:12 UTC) caused by simultaneous priming + customer burst; mitigated by throttling on lower-priority pools. No customer-facing SLO breaches.

Observations and metrics (high-level):
- Average GPU availability during pilot: 92% (target 95%). Preemption rate on demo nodes increased from 0.9% -> 1.4% during priming ramp.
- p50/p95/p99 latency delta (primed vs unprimed) for sample heavy-chat route: 5ms / -18% / -12% respectively. (See attached experiment dashboard for time series)
- Cost impact: priming adds ~0.07 GPU-hours per minute per primed-pool. For the pilot config (40 primed GPUs across 2 AZs), estimated incremental cost ~2.3% on monthly GPU consumption for the region.
- Cache hit behaviour: KV prefix cache warmed by priming produced ~11% token-level cache hits for repeated session patterns. Suggests higher value for LLM-chat-heavy workloads vs one-off generation calls.

What worked:
- Canary rollout logic prevented priming from firing during known high-burst windows (rule anchored to traffic annotations).
- Autoscaler integration respected priming locks so priming didn't compete with scaling up.
- Observability: new priming-specific metrics (primed_gpus, priming_success_rate, priming_last_heartbeat) were actionable during the first 24h.

What didn't / surprises:
- Preemption sensitivity: cheaper preemptible capacity in us-central created oscillations when priming tried to keep containers warm on those nodes. We need a stricter node-class affinity or fallback to non-preemptible for priming.
- Customer burst overlap: one customer bulk ingest overlapped a scheduled priming run (operator error in schedule config). Need guardrails so priming schedules are aware of customer-maintenance annotations.
- Edge variability: one AZ (us-midwest-2b) showed higher median temperature-based throttling from host telemetry - correlated with slightly lower priming_success_rate. Needs infra inspection.

Action items (owner / due):
- Add node-class affinity flag to priming controller to prefer non-preemptible pools (Samir / 2027-03-16).
- Backfill priming schedule with customer maintenance calendar and automated disable flag (Marta / 2027-03-14).
- Run host telemetry deep-dive for us-midwest-2b and file maintenance ticket if needed (Ethan / 2027-03-12).
- Update runbook to include priming throttle threshold and emergency disable endpoint (Priya / 2027-03-13).
- Post-mortem stub for the 2027-03-03 quota event (Olivia on-call + Priya / 2027-03-11).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is the 2.3% incremental cost acceptable vs the observed latency improvement for enterprise-tier customers? Proposal: enable priming only for routes tagged enterprise/high-latency-sensitive (requires product support).
- Should priming target session affinity instead of raw GPU counts to better capture repeated user sessions (more effective for chat).
- Can we experiment with partial-KV priming (warm top-k prefixes) to reduce GPU-hours while keeping latency gains? Need simulation from applied-ml.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight feature-flag API so sales/CS can request priming for specific customers during trials. Track cost center tagging.
- Triage: add alert for priming_success_rate < 85% that auto-posts to #infra-priming with a short summary.

Links & references:
- Experiment dashboard (internal): https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/priming/midwest-2027-02-22-03-08
- Linear issue for next-phase rollout: https://linear.app/INF/issue/PRIM-230-next-phase-scope
- GitHub PR with priming controller changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priming-experiments/pull/58

Meeting notes / timeline:
- 2027-03-03 04:12 UTC: quota oversubscription detected -> throttled lower-priority pools -> autoscaler reacted, 7% increased latency window. Root cause: priming + scheduled customer maintenance.
- 2027-03-05: priming schedule adjusted to avoid 03:00-06:00 UTC heavy batch windows; saw immediate reduction in small tail spikes.
- 2027-03-08: pilot end metrics exported, initial writeup drafted.

Next check-in: 2027-03-16 (two-week follow-up after remediation items).

Status: leaving as in_review until host telemetry item and affinity flag PR land.

Raw / informal scratch below (keep for audit):
- rough calc notes: 40 GPUs primed, each ~0.07 GPU-hrs/min => 40*0.07*60*24*14 = ~4700 GPU-hours over 14 days (note: this is raw and includes overlap; needs refine).
- overflow: consider throttling priming concurrency to 8 GPUs/min to smooth burst.
- TODO: call with product to scope enterprise-only rollout (Marta to schedule).

-- Priya
